proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $T$ is Noetherian, and by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] it has finite dimension. Its irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ are finite in number: [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite] gives a neighborhood meeting finitely many components at each point; a finite subcover exists since $T$ is quasi-compact. For each $i$ let $V_i=T\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$. This is an open subset with irreducible underlying space, contains the generic point $\eta_i$, and is contained in $C_i$. The $V_i$ are disjoint and their union contains all generic points.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1 (printed p.294)

proof.text: Only finitely many cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^r(K_a)$ are nonzero, by the bounded t-structure of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. Each admits a finite locally closed stratification on which it is lisse with locally constant ranks, by the final clause of that same node. For each $i$ and each such sheaf take the stratum containing $\eta_i$. A locally closed subset containing the generic point of an irreducible space contains an open neighborhood of that point: write it as an open subset of its closed closure, whose closure is all of $V_i$. Thus there is an open neighborhood $W_i\subseteq V_i$ of $\eta_i$ on which every one of the finitely many sheaves is lisse. Restriction is the exact pullback of that node. Each rank is constant on $W_i$, since a locally constant integer-valued function on an irreducible space is constant.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; finite-stratum constructible-heart characterization, followed by the elementary generic-stratum argument

proof.text: Shrink $W_i$ further so that $(W_i)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is regular. Indeed $k$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent]. Its J-2 property, as explicitly defined in [def-exc-excellent-ring], makes the regular locus of every finite-type $k$-algebra open. The reduced affine charts of $W_i$ are still finite-type $k$-algebras (quotient the coordinate rings by their nilradicals), so their regular loci glue to an open subset. This subset contains $\eta_i$: a reduced local ring at a minimal prime is a field, since it has just one prime ideal and its nilradical is zero. A field is regular of dimension zero by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Denote the resulting nonempty open by $U_i$. No assertion that $U_i$ is smooth over $k$ has been made.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1 (printed p.294)

proof.text: Put $U=\coprod_iU_i\subseteq T$ and $d_i=\dim U_i$. Each $d_i$ is a nonnegative finite integer by nonemptiness and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The complement $Z=T\setminus U$ contains no generic point. To check the strict dimension drop directly, an irreducible chain in $Z$ ends in an irreducible closed subset $F$ lying in some $C_i$, because the finite closed cover by the $C_i$ covers $F$. Since $\eta_i\notin Z$, $F\subsetneq C_i$. Appending $C_i$ gives a chain in $T$ one step longer. Consequently $\dim Z\leq\dim T-1$ if $Z$ is nonempty. Passing to its reduced closed subscheme changes no topological chain. This also proves that $Z$ is empty when $\dim T=0$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1 (printed p.294)

proof.text: Fix $X=U_i$ and $d=d_i$. At the coefficient field $\mathbf Q_\ell$, set $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\Omega_R=a_X^!R_k$, where $a_X$ is the structure map. By [lem-per-adic-exceptional-projection] this is a derived-complete bounded constructible integral object and its canonical derived reductions are $\nu_X^*a_{X,n}^!(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_k$, compatibly with the reduction tower. Apply [lem-per-finite-regular-reduction-dualizing] to $X$: it is separated finite-type with regular reduction and irreducible underlying space by the preceding construction. Thus the reduction tower of $\Omega_R[-2d]$ identifies with $N_n=\nu_X^*(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X(d)$, rank-one locally free sheaves in degree zero, with normalized Kummer transitions.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.4.1, Proposition 4.1.2, Theorem 5.1.1 and proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1; Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.7.19

proof.text: The compatible rank-one system $((\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X(d))_n$ defines a lisse $\mathbf Z_\ell$-sheaf $N$; [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] realizes it on the pro-etale site as the ordinary inverse limit $\varprojlim N_n$, locally free of rank one over the completed coefficient sheaf. The transitions $N_{n+1}\to N_n$ are epimorphisms, because they are reductions between normalized rank-one local systems. Therefore [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] identifies this ordinary limit in degree zero with the derived limit. On the other hand, [def-weil-derived-complete] identifies $\Omega_R[-2d]$ with a derived limit of the same tower. The uniqueness up to isomorphism in [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], clause 1, gives $\Omega_R\cong N[2d]$. Only an isomorphism is required; no canonical choice of a triangulated derived limit is asserted.

source.place: Lemmas 6.7.19--6.7.20 and Proposition 6.8.4; reconstruction from the normalized reduction tower

proof.text: Rationalize $N$ and pass to the common-field category; write $\mathcal O_i=(\mathbf Q_\ell,N[1/\ell])$. This is a rank-one lisse sheaf by [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] and [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. We verify that the image of $\Omega_R$ is the $\omega_X$ of the statement. For any finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ the scalar-extension comparison for $a_X^!$ in [lem-per-adic-exceptional-projection] identifies its integral value on the coefficient unit with $\Omega_R\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathcal O_E$. With the compact-support functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and raw rational Hom groups of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the integral adjunction bijections extend to rational Hom groups by tensoring with $E$; their inverses and naturality equations extend as well. Passing these compatible bijections to the filtered Hom colimits by [lem-coef-qbar-adjunction-hom-descent] gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(K,(\mathbf Q_\ell,\Omega_R[1/\ell]))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{X!}K,\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,k})$. Here the common-stage morphisms are precisely those of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. The adjunction of [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality] identifies the latter Hom group with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,\omega_X)$. Apply this natural bijection of represented Hom functors and its inverse to the two identity maps: naturality says the resulting maps are inverse. Thus the image of $\Omega_R$ is isomorphic to $\omega_X$. It follows from the preceding step that $\omega_X\cong\mathcal O_i[2d]$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; rationalization and common finite-stage adjunction

proof.text: For a lisse sheaf $M$ on $X$ put $F(M)=R\mathcal Hom(M,\mathcal O_i)$. The evaluation pairing induces $M^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_i\to F(M)$. This is an isomorphism in degree zero: at a common finite coefficient field, take a pro-etale cover trivializing both locally finite free sheaves; it becomes the equality between the matrix dual of a finite free module with values in a free line and its ordinary dual tensored with that line. Derived internal Hom restricts to these slice sites by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The actual integral evaluation and tensor--Hom adjunction are those of [lem-per-adic-closed-constructible], so these local evaluations give the specified adic comparison after rationalization. The dual and tensor cohomology calculations in [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus] identify its source with the asserted degree-zero sheaf. All maps are evaluation-defined and hence agree after finite coefficient extension; they give the same isomorphism in the common-stage category. In particular $F$ sends every lisse sheaf to its linear dual tensored with $\mathcal O_i$, in degree zero.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4 and Remark 6.8.15; local finite-free evaluation calculation

proof.text:
For a bounded $L$ with lisse cohomology let $F(L)=R\mathcal Hom(L,\mathcal O_i)$. This functor is contravariantly exact and reverses shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Induct on the number of degrees in an interval containing the nonzero cohomology of $L$. The zero object is immediate. If $b$ is the highest nonzero degree, use the standard truncation triangle
$$A=\tau^{\le b-1}L\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow\mathcal H^b(L)[-b]\longrightarrow A[1]$$
of the bounded t-structure in [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. Applying $F$ gives a triangle with first term $(\mathcal H^bL)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_i[b]$, by the preceding step, and third term $F(A)$. Inductively $F(A)$ has no cohomology below $-b+1$ and has cohomology $(\mathcal H^{-r}A)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_i$ in degree $r$. The cohomology exact sequence therefore identifies $\mathcal H^{-b}F(L)$ with $(\mathcal H^bL)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_i$ and identifies $\mathcal H^rF(L)$ with $\mathcal H^rF(A)$ for $r>-b$; both sides vanish for $r<-b$. This proves $\mathcal H^rF(L)\cong(\mathcal H^{-r}L)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_i$ for every $r$, including gaps in the cohomological interval.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; elementary bounded standard-truncation induction after the lisse evaluation calculation

proof.text:
By the definition of $D_X$ in [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality] and $\omega_X\cong\mathcal O_i[2d]$, the internal-Hom shift isomorphism gives $D_XL\cong F(L)[2d]$. Since $\mathcal H^r(B[2d])=\mathcal H^{r+2d}(B)$, the preceding formula yields
$$\mathcal H^r(D_XL)\cong(\mathcal H^{-r-2d}L)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_i.$$
Its right side is lisse by the dual and tensor assertions of [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus]. At every geometric point its fibre is the ordinary dual of the finite-dimensional fibre of $\mathcal H^{-r-2d}L$, tensored with a one-dimensional space. Such a space vanishes exactly when the original fibre does. Joint conservativity of geometric fibres in [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] then gives the asserted equivalence of vanishing. The argument applied to each $U_i$ proves every clause, including nonreduced schemes and imperfect fields.

title: Generic lisse local form of the relative dualizing complex
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $T$ be a nonempty separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use $\mathcal C_W=D^b_c(W,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], its standard bounded t-structure and cohomology of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], and $\omega_W$ and $D_W$ with relative dimension normalization from [lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality]. A lisse sheaf means a finite-rank adic sheaf in the sense of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]; linear dual and tensor use [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus]. Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

For any finite family $K_1,\ldots,K_s\in\mathcal C_T$, there exists a dense open $U\subseteq T$ containing every generic point of $T$, with a finite disjoint decomposition into nonempty open subschemes $U=\coprod_\alpha U_\alpha$, each with irreducible underlying space and dimension $d_\alpha\ge0$, such that all $\mathcal H^r(K_a)|_{U_\alpha}$ are lisse of constant rank. Its reduced closed complement has dimension strictly smaller than $\dim T$ (and may be empty). For each $\alpha$ there is a rank-one lisse sheaf $\mathcal O_\alpha$ and an isomorphism $\omega_{U_\alpha}\cong\mathcal O_\alpha[2d_\alpha]$.

For any $L\in\mathcal C_{U_\alpha}$ with lisse cohomology sheaves, there are isomorphisms
$$\mathcal H^r(D_{U_\alpha}L)\cong\bigl(\mathcal H^{-r-2d_\alpha}(L)\bigr)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_\alpha\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z).$$
In particular the right side is lisse and is zero if and only if $\mathcal H^{-r-2d_\alpha}(L)$ is zero. The assertion does not require $k$ to be perfect or $U_\alpha$ to be smooth over $k$.
